$comment: A CATALOGUE ENTRY, NOT AN AUTHORITY. Two repositories were read. The first is a BARE workflow -- `ios/` and `android/` prebuild output committed -- so this profile is three lanes wearing one name, and its host note says so rather than flattening them; its `lint`, `dev`, `run` and toolchain rows are still that inventory's. The second, the `apps/mobile` lane of Market, the maintainer's private Next.js + Expo monorepo (a managed Expo lane in a Next.js + Expo monorepo, read at 765c0d7 on 2026-11-09), is the maintained reference the `build`, `test`, `ui-test`, `archive` and `coverage` rows are cited to, each a command that repository's own nen/contract.json runs (zheref/nen#502).

markers.why: the manifest, identified by its `expo` key -- `app.json` alone is far too common a filename to be a marker.
or `app.config.ts`: the dynamic manifest, same key.
identifies an Expo project on its own: the EAS build-profile file, which the reference's `archive` row reads (Market apps/mobile/eas.json:6-26).
`ios/` AND `android/` both present means the BARE workflow -- prebuild output is committed, and the native lanes are real.

the other half of the same conjunction, and it is a marker for the same reason: `android/` beside `ios/` is what makes the workflow BARE. Stated as its own row because the rule is an AND, and a table that names only one of the two directories reads as if either alone were enough.

hostNote: SPLIT BY LANE, and the single `hosts` row cannot say it: `expo start` and `expo lint` run anywhere; `expo run:ios` needs macOS with Xcode and CocoaPods; `expo run:android` needs a JDK, the Android SDK and `node` on PATH for the Gradle configuration. The declaration narrows `run` to `darwin` for the iOS lane; the pack refuses to narrow it for a verb whose android half runs everywhere. `archive` is as host-locked as the platform it builds: the reference's local EAS build targets iOS and needs macOS with Xcode and CocoaPods. `ui-test` needs the Maestro CLI installed on whatever host runs it.
scaffoldNote: `app.json`, `package.json`, an `app/` route skeleton and nen/contract.json. NATIVE DIRECTORIES ARE NOT TEMPLATED; an `expo prebuild` is a printed post-step.

detect.declaredOnly: Detection is a marker match, not a spawned command: `app.json` / `app.config.{js,ts}` carrying an `expo` key, or an `eas.json`; `ios/` AND `android/` present means the bare workflow.

build.why: THE BUILD-ONLY INVOCATION, AND IT LAUNCHES NOTHING. The reference's `build` script is `expo export --platform ios --platform android --output-dir dist`: Metro bundles both native targets to Hermes bytecode in `dist/` without starting an app or a simulator. That is the distinction this row exists for -- `expo run:ios` / `expo run:android` build AND launch, and are this profile's `run` row, never this one. A native binary is `archive`'s. `{pm}` is the repository's package manager, from its own `packageManager` field.

test.why: Jest with the `jest-expo` preset and React Native Testing Library -- the Expo-target logic layer of the `react-uzf-v1` quality baseline. The reference's jest.config.js selects `__tests__/` (screens from `app/`, which expo-router would otherwise route as pages) and `src/`, and its suite renders a real screen. `jest` is invoked through the project's own dependency, never a global install.

ui-test.why: Maestro flows under `.maestro/`, the Expo-target UI layer of the quality baseline, run against a DEV-CLIENT build (`expo-dev-client`; the flow's `appId` is the app's bundle id). PRECONDITIONS THIS ROW CANNOT SATISFY FOR ITSELF, and nen asserts rather than performs: the dev client installed on a booted simulator or emulator, and Metro serving on :8081 (this profile's `dev` row). The Maestro CLI is a host install, not a package dependency.

lint.why: Flat ESLint 9 with `eslint-config-expo/flat`, ignoring `dist/*`. `expo` is invoked through the project's own dependency, never a global install.

typecheck.unsupported: Neither repository's declaration runs a type check. The first configures TypeScript and never runs `tsc`: no script, no workflow. The reference carries a `typecheck` script (`tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`) that its root fans out to through turbo, but its nen/contract.json seats no `typecheck` row on the mobile lane, so there is no declared run to cite. The pack seats no command a reference's declaration does not run; a repository that does check its types states that command here.
typecheck.source: food-diary/tsconfig.json; package.json:5-13, :53; Market apps/mobile/package.json:14; Market package.json:14 (root); turbo.json:16-17; nen/contract.json:16-84

archive.why: A LOCAL EAS BUILD. The reference's `archive` script is `eas build --local --platform ios --profile simulator --non-interactive --output dist-archive/market-ios-simulator.tar.gz`: a Release iOS simulator `.app` built on this machine from the `simulator` profile in `eas.json`, linked to the EAS project `app.json`'s `extra.eas.projectId` names. The pack seats the SCRIPT, not its flags, because the profile name and the output path are that repository's choices. The simulator profile needs no signing credentials; a device or store build does. PRECONDITIONS ASSERTED, NEVER PERFORMED: Xcode, CocoaPods, fastlane, a UTF-8 locale, and an EAS sign-in (`eas login` or `EXPO_TOKEN`), because a local build still checks the account. `eas-cli` is the project's own devDependency.

release.unsupported: Nothing in the reference runs `eas submit` or fastlane. Its `eas.json` carries an empty `submit.production` block and no script submits a build; its declaration still carries `detect`'s unreplaced seat for `release`, which is not a ruling of its own. There is no observed publication step to cite.

dev.why: The Metro dev server. `expo start --web` is the same verb with the web target, and is the declaration's argument to add.

run.why: The repository declares three forms: `expo run:ios`, `expo run:ios --device` and `expo run:android`. `{platform}` selects the lane and `--device` is the declaration's own extra argument; neither native lane is the other's default, so the pack templates rather than picks. THESE BUILD AND LAUNCH, which is why they are `run` and never `build` (the export).

deploy.unsupported: No deployment target of any kind in either repository: the reference's declaration names no `targets` (its `deploy` row is still `detect`'s unreplaced seat, not a ruling of its own). An EAS build profile is a build configuration, not a destination.

coverage.why: The same Jest run as `test`, instrumented. The reference's jest.config.js collects from `app/`, `src/` and `plugins/` and writes the `text`, `lcov` and `json-summary` reporters to the lane's own `coverage/` directory, which its declaration names as this row's artifact. `jest` is invoked through the project's own dependency.

tools.why: THE JS LANE ONLY, and it is the same one install nen performs anywhere: `{packageManager}` comes from the DECLARATION'S own `packageManager` pin, never from this pack. Everything else here is verify-only, and this row is the clearest case in the inventory for a per-lane toolchain. Node -- verify-only. Expo CLI -- installer `npx`, which installs NOTHING GLOBALLY: `expo` is invoked through the project's own dependency, and Expo itself warns against a global install; the row exists to say so rather than leave a reader guessing. iOS lane -- Xcode, simulator runtimes and CocoaPods, all verify-only, exactly as the xcode-ios profile. Android lane -- a JDK and Android SDK components as the gradle-android profile, PLUS `node` on PATH for a Gradle SYNC, which is a verify-only probe most readers would not expect.

warmup.why: The git steps are stack-independent and run regardless. The verification half delegates to this profile's own `build` and `test` rows, both of which carry a command -- and `build` is the export, which launches nothing, so verifying a warm tree never starts an app.
warmup.source: this profile's own build and test rows

expo-cli.why: NOTHING TO INSTALL GLOBALLY. `expo` is invoked through the project's own dependency, and Expo itself warns against a global install; this entry exists to state that rather than leave a reader to discover it. The observed project is Expo SDK 53 with expo-router 5 on React Native 0.79.5, and the CLI version travels with the project, so the pack states no host minimum.

node.why: The repository pins no `engines` range, so the pack states presence only. Node is verify-only here for the same reason it is everywhere: a Node install is a system-wide decision with five common answers. The Android lane additionally needs it ON PATH for the Gradle sync.

reportDefault.$comment: ADVISORY ONLY, and the one thing `nen shu coverage` may say about a report location it was not given. That verb parses the report a DECLARATION names under the coverage verb's `artifacts`; when a repository names none, this path (or this reason) is quoted in the refusal and NEVER opened. `path: null` is the honest answer for a stack whose report location does not exist or is not conventional.
reportDefault.why: REPO-ROOT-RELATIVE, AND THAT IS WHY IT NAMES A LANE DIRECTORY. The coverage row writes an LCOV tracefile in the lane's OWN `coverage/` directory, and `artifacts` is resolved against the repository root, so the path recorded is the reference's lane written out in full. A single-app Expo repository whose lane is the root writes `coverage/lcov.info`; a `json-summary` reporter writes `coverage-summary.json` beside it, and nen reads either.
reportDefault.source: this profile's own `coverage` row (Market apps/mobile/jest.config.js:17-18; nen/contract.json:80-82)

deployDefault.why: No deployment target of any kind is observed, so there is no conventional name to propose. An EAS build profile is a build configuration, not a destination.
deployDefault.source: Market nen/contract.json:172; food-diary (inventory sweep); this profile's own `deploy` row

notes: Expo's selected native platform reuses that platform's device declaration: the xcode-ios JSON extractor for an iOS target and the gradle-android text extractor for an Android target. Expo contributes no third discovery schema and nen chooses neither platform.

PRECONDITIONS ASSERTED, NEVER PERFORMED: `pod install` for the iOS lane; a JDK plus the Android SDK AND `node` on PATH for the Gradle lane; and a booted simulator. The repository's own helper hardcodes booting an `iPhone 16 Pro` (food-diary/start-ios.sh:5, :12) -- nen asserts a simulator exists and never boots one.
The native lanes' toolchains are the xcode-ios and gradle-android profiles' rows, not copies of them. Duplicating those entries here would create two places to fix the same fact.
